title: Visualization of Moiré Superlattice Induced by Heterostrain in MoS2
content: Two-dimensional (2D) moiré systems possess a variety of emergent properties that are absent in their individual layers, including superconductivity [1], moiré excitons [2], magnetism [3], and interfacial ferroelectricity [4]. Most moiré systems to date have been realized through the rotational misalignment and lattice mismatch between adjacent layers. Heterostrain, by individually straining the topmost layers with respect to the other, offers a powerful approach to enhance moiré tunability [5]; however, its experimental realization remains challenging. Recent experimental advances in process-induced strain-engineering technique have enabled controlled strain application in 2D materials through lithographic patterning of stressor thin films [6], providing a versatile platform to engineer and tailor the moiré material properties. Despite these advancements, a real-space characterization of how stressor-film induced strain influences the local structural arrangements and moiré superlattices is lacking. Such insights are crucial for investigating the response of 2D materials to mechanical strain for advanced electronic and optoelectronic devices.
